subject: general
question: In a frequency curve, what is plotted on vertical axis?
solution:
The correct answer is** Class frequencies**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Class frequencies:**

 
 
• In a frequency curve, the vertical axis (y-axis) represents the class frequencies, which indicate the number of observations within each class interval.
 
• Class frequencies are crucial in financial enterprises for visualizing the distribution of variables such as sales, expenses, or investment returns over specified intervals.
 
• This visualization helps in identifying trends, patterns, and outliers, aiding decision-making processes and strategic planning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Class limits:**

 
 
• Class limits define the boundaries of each class interval but are not plotted on the vertical axis.
 
• They are used to categorize data into different intervals, which is essential for constructing frequency distributions but not directly for plotting on the y-axis.
 
 
 
• **Cumulative frequencies:**
 
 
• Cumulative frequencies represent the sum of all class frequencies up to a certain class interval.
 
• These are typically plotted in an Ogive graph and not in a standard frequency curve, where individual class frequencies are plotted.
 
 
 
• **Class boundaries:**
 
 
• Class boundaries are the actual limits used to separate classes but are not plotted on the vertical axis.
 
• They are essential for defining the precise range of data points within each class interval but do not represent the frequency of data points.
